newsitem.title: UK: British Telecom to run UK's military phone system.
newsitem.headline: British Telecom to run UK's military phone system.

text.p: The British government said Wednesday it had chosen a consortium led by British Telecommunications Plc to take over and run its armed forces telephone network in Britain.
Other members of the consortium include Lockheed Martin and British firm GEC-Marconi, a unit of Britain's General Electric Co. Plc.
The change is designed to modernise services and to cut the armed forces' telephone bill by 15 percent to about 85 million British pounds ($140 million) a year, government officials said.
Defence Secretary Michael Portillo said in a written parliamentary answer that the initial contract would be worth 700 million pounds ($1.15 billion).
Ministry of Defence officials and British Telecom later said the overall value of the contract would be closer to 1 billion pounds ($1.6 billion) once user tariffs were taken into account.
The award is still subject to final negotiations but the officials told reporters the government expects a contract will be signed in time for British Telecom to start work next April.
